papers.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT

summary.en: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer reuses keys and values as memory across depths and loops; U-MoLT beats OLMo3 with 1.7x CE token efficiency at 700M and +2.1 points on 10-task accuracy at 3B MoE.
summary.zh: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer 用 Mixture-of-Loops Attention 把 KV 当作跨深度和循环复用记忆，其 U-MoLT 变体在 400B token 预训练中于 700M 模型上比 OLMo3 达到 1.7 倍的验证交叉熵 token 效率，3B MoE 困惑度降低 0.75、10 项任务准确率提升 2.1 个百分点。

papers.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
papers.abstract: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical pretraining, staged supervised fine-tuning, and adaptive reinforcement learning. Across this curriculum, progressive supervised refinement and adaptive reinforcement learning yield consistent stage-wise gains, substantially advancing both specialized visual understanding and medical language capabilities. Evaluated against 77 competing models across 238 clinical tasks spanning 61 public and 13 private multi-center benchmarks in more than 40 modalities, Sage-Med-Preview achieves an average score of 58.26% on the 31 public multimodal benchmarks. It outperforms the state-of-the-art open-source medical model Hulu-Med-235B-A22B at 50.99% and the general scientific model Intern-S2-Preview at 52.24%, and approaches the advanced proprietary model GPT-6.2-Sol across multiple tasks such as comprehensive multimodal understanding, report generation, and visual grounding. Although substantial challenges remain in complex medical reasoning and multi-step clinical workflows, this report provides empirical evidence, actionable data and training recipes, and a rigorous benchmark toward scalable clinical multimodal intelligence.

summary.en: Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter (3B activated) medical MLLM trained via curated 322.7M-record data and a progressive pretraining-to-SFT-to-RL curriculum, scores 58.26% on 31 public multimodal benchmarks, beating Hulu-Med-235B-A22B (50.99%) and Intern-S2-Preview (52.24%).
summary.zh: Sage-Med-Preview 是 35B 参数（激活 3B）的医学多模态模型，用 3.227 亿条候选数据分阶段筛选结合医学预训练、分阶段监督微调与自适应强化学习的渐进课程训练，在 31 个公开多模态基准上均分 58.26%，超过 Hulu-Med-235B-A22B 的 50.99% 和 Intern-S2-Preview 的 52.24%。

papers.title: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) scale model capacity by increasing both parameter count and computation. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants expand parameter capacity while keeping per-token computation roughly fixed, but still require substantial parameter storage. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT), which reuses parameters rather than adding them: a weight-shared loop repeatedly applies the middle layers, while sparse experts allocate parameter capacity across tokens. This design deepens the network without adding parameters, freeing the parameter budget for other uses, such as more experts or more distinct layers. It also allocates compute dynamically, varying the number of passes across noise levels. Experiments show that DyLoMo-DiT makes more effective use of parameter and compute budgets, with further gains from assigning more passes to low-noise steps. On ImageNet $256\times256$, DyLoMo-DiT reduces FID by 11-24% relative to DiT and 36-56% relative to DiT-MoE at matched parameter and compute budgets. For text-to-image generation, a scaled DyLoMo-DiT achieves a higher GenEval score than FLUX.1 (0.714 vs. 0.673), with less than one tenth of its active parameters (1.05B vs. 12B).
papers.comment: 46 pages, 29 figures, 33 tables. Code, weights and project page: https://oneboxcream.github.io/DyLoMo-DiT/

summary.en: DyLoMo-DiT reuses parameters via weight-shared loops over middle layers plus sparse experts and noise-level-dependent pass counts; it cuts FID 11-24% vs DiT and 36-56% vs DiT-MoE, and beats FLUX.1 on GenEval (0.714 vs 0.673) with 1.05B active parameters.
summary.zh: DyLoMo-DiT 复用参数而非新增参数：权重共享循环重复施加中间层，稀疏专家按 token 分配容量，并按噪声水平动态调整循环次数。在 ImageNet 256×256 上，同参数与计算预算下 FID 相比 DiT 降 11–24%、相比 DiT-MoE 降 36–56%；文生图 GenEval 得分 0.714 超过 FLUX.1 的 0.673，活跃参数仅 1.05B（对比 12B）。

papers.title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Real-time autoregressive video generators stream minutes of video and accept new prompts on the fly, but struggle to keep people, objects, and places consistent over a long interactive story. Agent systems provide such memory for offline multi-shot generation, yet they read the whole script in advance, plan each shot before generating it, and regenerate failed shots, which a live stream does not allow. We present Agentic LongLive, an asynchronous agentic memory for long video generation. A memory agent on separate GPUs reads only the prompts revealed so far, never the generated video, and keeps a text state and evolving images for every person, object, and scene. From this entity memory it composes a global image and a per-shot memory image, which an auxiliary GPU prefills into the generator's attention sink before the next shot starts, and writes entity cards for the prompts that name them, so the video never waits for memory and video errors are not written back. A small language model, trained with reinforcement learning and an image reward calibrated using downstream video outcomes, decides what to remember before the next prompt is known. On LongStory-Online, a new benchmark of 25 stories (857 shots) revealed one shot at a time, Agentic LongLive improves persistent-state accuracy of LongLive-2.0, its base generator, by 26.3 points, protagonist identity by 44.9, and revisited-place consistency by 40.4, at about 1% extra generation time on H100. The full system streams faster than real time on one 8xB200 node with the generator in BF16 (34.3 FPS), keeps image quality stable over 14-minute stories, and improves identity on two MiniMax-H3 generators, one of which, LongLive-H3, also runs in real time with it. To our knowledge, it is the first real-time video generator with text and image memory kept by an LLM agent.

summary.en: Agentic LongLive keeps entity memory on separate GPUs and prefills it into the generator's attention sink, raising LongLive-2.0 persistent-state accuracy by 26.3 points with about 1% extra generation time.
summary.zh: Agentic LongLive 用独立 GPU 上的记忆 agent 以文本状态和实体图像维护人物、物体、场景一致性，并通过辅助 GPU 预填充注意力 sink，使 LongLive-2.0 在 LongStory-Online 上持久状态准确率提升 26.3 点、主角身份提升 44.9 点、重访地点一致性提升 40.4 点，额外耗时约 1%。

papers.title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
papers.abstract: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical context and user intent, and reassess whether prior digital actions remain valid. Whether current agents can reliably handle these changes remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce EgoUseBench, a benchmark for evaluating Ego Use across three interaction settings with different levels of first-person context. Computer-Use relies on explicit instructions, Offline Ego Use provides prerecorded first-person context before execution, and Online Ego Use provides continuous observations as user intent evolves. Based on over 74 hours of real-world first-person recordings, we construct 693 tasks across the three interaction settings. To capture task evolution, we track first-person observations, user requirements, and website state separately. We further group tasks by how information changes during execution, resulting in three types: Graft (revised user requirements), Refresh (new first-person observations), and Clarify (agent-initiated information seeking). We evaluate advanced models and find that average success rates in Online Ego Use are 26.3% lower than in Computer-Use. This result reveals the difficulty of keeping task execution aligned with evolving first-person context and user intent.

summary.en: EgoUseBench builds 693 tasks from 74+ hours of real first-person recordings to evaluate computer-use agents across three settings; Online Ego Use success rates are 26.3% lower than Computer-Use.
summary.zh: EgoUseBench 基于超过 74 小时的真实第一人称录像构建 693 个任务，在 Computer-Use、Offline Ego Use 和 Online Ego Use 三种设定下评测计算机使用智能体，并发现 Online Ego Use 的平均成功率比 Computer-Use 低 26.3%。

papers.title: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
papers.abstract: Code-driven video generation asks a coding agent to write and run rendering programs. This gives exact control over typography, data visualizations, synchronized audio, and multi-shot scenes, and it leaves an editable project behind. A program that exits cleanly can still render overlapping labels, a camera aimed away from its subject, broken object interactions, or narration that drifts out of sync, and none of these raise a runtime error. Feeding rendered frames and audio back into the coding session bloats its long-horizon context, while critiquing only the finished full-resolution render turns early design mistakes into costly rewrites. We introduce VibeVideoAgent, a training-free framework that lets coding agents inspect their drafts throughout production. Multimodal perception runs in short-lived contexts kept apart from the coder and returns compact, grounded Findings. Seven primitives operate on a unified multi-clock representation of assets and drafts: they explore media from coarse to fine, verify quoted requirements with evidence from every required modality, compare a draft with a reference or an earlier revision on separate clocks, and measure stream signals locally. A lightweight staged protocol has the agent test its riskiest decision on a minimal preview first. On all 239 VibeVideoBench tasks, with matched agent runtimes and a fixed perception model, VibeVideoAgent improves holistic audiovisual quality (L3) for Claude Opus 5.5 (4.03 -> 4.43, while L2 rubric compliance rises from 98.87% to 99.35%), GPT-6 Astra (4.03 -> 4.27), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (3.97 -> 4.10), with the largest gains in audio-visual synchronization (up to +0.56). Controlled ablations show that each component contributes, and trajectory audits show that the granularity of code edits governs the trade-off between rubric adherence and perceptual quality.

summary.en: VibeVideoAgent is a training-free framework letting coding agents inspect drafts via short-lived multimodal perception and seven primitives over a unified multi-clock representation; on 239 VibeVideoBench tasks it lifts Claude Opus 5.5's L3 from 4.03 to 4.43, with audio-visual sync gains up to +0.56.
summary.zh: VibeVideoAgent 是一个免训练框架，让编程智能体在生成过程中通过短时上下文的多模态感知检查草稿，并借助统一多时钟表示上的七种原语返回精简的 Findings 反馈；在 239 个 VibeVideoBench 任务上，Claude Opus 5.5 的整体视听质量 L3 由 4.03 升至 4.43，音画同步最多提升 0.56。

papers.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for enhanced robustness and execution efficiency. In simulated environments, PyRUA-Dex achieves SOTA on Bench2Dex with a score of 72.9 and reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, PyRUA-Dex learns to play piano, write calligraphy, and other tasks efficiently: learning a new piece from sheet music takes as little as 30 minutes. These results suggest that PyRUA-Dex is an effective framework for developing dexterous manipulation policies with coding agents in the absence of high quality dexterous manipulation demonstrations.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 9 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://vme0522.github.io/PyRUA-Dex/

summary.en: PyRUA-Dex lets coding agents build programmatic dexterous bimanual policies without demonstrations, distilling parallel exploration into a task library and program, then refining with randomized layouts; it scores 72.9 SOTA on Bench2Dex and 81.0% on DexJoCo.
summary.zh: PyRUA-Dex 让编码智能体无需高质量示教即可为双手灵巧操作编写程序化策略：先并行探索技能与组合方式，再由蒸馏智能体压缩成任务库和一段程序，最后用随机布局提升鲁棒性与效率；在 Bench2Dex 上取得 72.9 的 SOTA 分数，DexJoCo 完全随机化下成功率 81.0%，真机 22 自由度双手平台学一首钢琴曲最快约 30 分钟。

papers.title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
papers.abstract: Image editing models can follow a wide range of instructions, but video editing models still lag behind, limited in part by the difficulty of collecting paired source and edited videos. Is it possible to transfer advanced image editing capabilities to video editors without new paired videos? We introduce Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), which improves pretrained video editors and expands them to new editing tasks using an image editor. It enables efficient post-training with no architectural changes and no new videos, using only individual images. Our key idea is to let the video editor role-play as an image editor: it edits an image as a one-frame video, with the image editor guiding the video editor's predictions at each denoising step. Although the video editor sees only single images during training, at test time it applies the improved and expanded capabilities to whole video clips while preserving temporal consistency. To push the boundaries of video editing, we introduce OpenVE++, an extension of OpenVE-Bench that adds four new editing tasks useful for video production, including action changes, expression changes, body movements, and scene relighting. Our experiments across three different video editors show that I2VT improves existing editing capabilities and expands them to new tasks, and our models achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on both OpenVE-Bench and OpenVE++.

summary.en: I2VT transfers image editing to video editors by having them role-play as image editors on single frames, guided per denoising step, achieving SOTA on OpenVE-Bench and the new OpenVE++.
summary.zh: I2VT 让视频编辑器在训练时以单帧图像扮演图像编辑器，由图像编辑器逐去噪步引导预测，无需配对视频即可把图像编辑能力迁移并扩展到动作、表情、肢体运动和场景重打光等任务，在 OpenVE-Bench 与 OpenVE++ 上取得 SOTA。

papers.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) that continue improving after deployment (e.g., recursive self-improvement) offer a promising path toward general intelligence. Current test-time methods pursue this goal on unlabeled questions, primarily relying on self-consistency: they generate independent solutions and use majority voting to select an answer or construct training targets. This leaves earlier reasoning unused at inference and can reinforce an incorrect majority during training. Humans instead build on earlier attempts to preserve useful reasoning, correct mistakes and improve their problem-solving strategies. Following this principle, we propose Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement (TT-RSI), a label-free framework for improving LLMs at test time through two mutually reinforcing components: (1) In-Context RSI repeatedly re-solves each question using the full previous solution as a reference, letting the model decide whether and how to use it so that inference compute builds on earlier reasoning. (2) In-Weight RSI distills successive refinements into the model's weights, enabling progress beyond an initially wrong majority and theoretically bringing the first attempt toward the model's infinite-step refinement limit. The updated model answers better and refines more effectively, generating stronger references for subsequent training. Extensive experiments show that TT-RSI improves average accuracy by +13.89% over the base model and outperforms the strongest self-consistency-based method by +4.79% under the same test-time scaling budget.

summary.en: TT-RSI is a label-free test-time framework that re-solves questions with full prior solutions (In-Context RSI) and distills refinements into weights (In-Weight RSI). It beats the base model by +13.89% and the strongest self-consistency method by +4.79%.
summary.zh: TT-RSI 是一个无需标签的测试时框架，通过 In-Context RSI 反复参考先前完整解答重解问题、In-Weight RSI 将逐步改进蒸馏进模型权重，实现推理计算累积与纠错；平均准确率较基座模型提升 +13.89%，在同等测试时算力预算下比最强自一致性方法高 +4.79%。

orgs.name: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts
papers.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables foundation models to perform unseen tasks from context without parameter updates. In robotic manipulation, a human video provides the context that specifies how a task should be performed. However, scaling human-video ICL on world-action models (WAMs) faces two challenges: task-level human-robot pairs are not temporally aligned with robot actions, and standard action losses allow policies to rely on initial-scene or task-identity shortcuts rather than tracking the context. We present Entangle, an in-context world-action model that maps a single human video and current robot observations to future visual states and executable actions. To scale temporally aligned training data, we convert recorded robot videos into matched human contexts via video-to-video generation, supplemented by real paired recordings. For model training, we combine variable-length video windows with an intra-task contrastive objective that distinguishes the paired action trajectory from other executions of the same task, preventing task-identity shortcuts. Without task-specific fine-tuning, Entangle improves steadily as aligned training data scales, reaching an average score of 83.5/100 across six unseen tasks on an Astribot S1 robot, and achieves a 69.5% average success rate on seven unseen RoboTwin tasks, outperforming Zero-WAM by 22.6 percentage points. Under Context-OOD, although trained only on scene-aligned pairs, Entangle transfers context-specified behaviors across rearranged layouts and substituted tools. Project page at https://entangle-robotics.github.io/
papers.comment: 26 pages, 13 figures, including the appendix. Project page at https://entangle-robotics.github.io/

summary.en: Entangle converts robot videos into matched human contexts via video-to-video generation and trains an in-context world-action model with variable-length windows and intra-task contrastive objectives, scoring 83.5/100 on six unseen Astribot S1 tasks and 69.5% success on seven unseen RoboTwin tasks, 22.6 points above Zero-WAM.
summary.zh: Entangle 用视频到视频生成把机器人视频转成匹配的人类示范上下文，并结合变长视频窗口与任务内对比目标训练上下文世界-动作模型，在 Astribot S1 的六个未见任务上平均得分 83.5/100，在七个 RoboTwin 未见任务上平均成功率 69.5%，比 Zero-WAM 高 22.6 个百分点。

papers.title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
papers.abstract: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the heterogeneous visual representations used for understanding and generation. To address this challenge, we introduce Integral, which converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space across the two capabilities. Integral implements this design through two complementary components. Abstraction Fusion constructs shared visual tokens by aggregating hierarchical representations from the frozen vision encoder, while Block-wise MoT introduces a lightweight generative stream that interacts with the vision-language model only at block boundaries. Our approach effectively preserves the pretrained understanding capability while extending it to strong visual generation. Controlled comparisons further demonstrate that sharing visual representations between understanding and generation substantially improves generative learning compared with using a separate visual representation space, despite comparable reconstruction fidelity. These results suggest that representations learned by pretrained vision-language models already provide an effective foundation for visual generation.

summary.en: Integral turns a pretrained VLM into a unified multimodal model: Abstraction Fusion builds shared visual tokens from a frozen encoder's hierarchy, and Block-wise MoT adds a lightweight generative stream at block boundaries, preserving understanding while enabling strong generation; shared representations beat separate ones.
summary.zh: Integral 将预训练视觉语言模型转为统一多模态模型：Abstraction Fusion 聚合冻结视觉编码器的层级表征构建共享视觉 token，Block-wise MoT 在块边界接入轻量生成流；在保持理解能力的同时实现强图像生成，共享视觉表征比独立表征显著提升生成学习。

papers.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
papers.abstract: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. We study the alternative, \emph{model-driven} context management, in which the model itself decides when and what to compact through a context API. We gave models control over their own context in \nooa, NVIDIA's open source agent harness, and compared the two strategies on document research and machine learning engineering across context budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. Models that use the context API effectively reach higher accuracy, often with fewer input tokens, especially at tight budgets: \textbf{GPT 6.1 nearly triples its score at a 32K budget} on OfficeQA Pro v2 (21\%~$\rightarrow$~56\%), and \textbf{Kimi gains with up to 41\% fewer input tokens}. Models differ widely, however, in how often they use the API, how aggressively they compact, and when they start compacting, and prompt changes shift that timing. Finally, we show that \textbf{inference engines can make model-driven edits cheaper}: by reusing the KV cache of the unchanged suffix after an edit, \textbf{we cut prefill compute by up to 15\% per request with no measurable change in accuracy}. Together, these results point to a new co-design frontier: models trained to manage their own context, served by inference engines that support KV cache editing.

summary.en: In NVIDIA's NOOA harness, models decide via a context API when and what to compact; GPT 6.1 nearly tripled OfficeQA Pro v2 accuracy at 32K budget (21%→56%), Kimi used up to 41% fewer input tokens, and reusing KV cache cut prefill compute up to 15%.
summary.zh: 在 NVIDIA 开源 agent harness NOOA 中让模型通过 context API 自主决定何时压缩上下文，在 8K–512K 预算的文档研究与 ML 工程任务上与 harness 驱动的压缩对比：GPT 6.1 在 32K 预算下 OfficeQA Pro v2 准确率由 21% 升至 56%，Kimi 输入 token 最多减少 41%；复用 KV cache 的未变后缀可将 prefill 计算降低最多 15% 且精度无损。

papers.title: DocSEAM: Bidirectional Cross-Page Encoding for Multi-Page Document Understanding
papers.abstract: Multi-page document vision-language models encode each page independently, creating a feature-level discontinuity at page boundaries: visual tokens are formed without access to content on adjacent pages, and the language model must reason over these page representations formed in isolation. We introduce DocSEAM (Document Selective Enrichment via Anchored Masking), a lightweight module inserted between a pretrained vision encoder and the language model that injects the inductive bias of local cross-page context into visual representations. For each page, DocSEAM forms a local triplet with its two neighbors, applies center-anchored masked self-attention with directional salience gates to fuse information from neighbor pages, and returns only the enriched center-page tokens, leaving the visual token count unchanged. After a supervised cross-page warm-up and multi-page fine-tuning with DocSEAM frozen, our 9B-parameter model achieves state-of-the-art results among the evaluated open-weight models of up to 10B parameters on five multi-page document VQA benchmarks. We further show that under controlled re-pagination, DocSEAM reduces sensitivity to boundary placement and improves cross-page span localization

summary.en: DocSEAM inserts a lightweight module between the vision encoder and LLM, fusing neighboring pages via center-anchored masked attention; the 9B model achieves SOTA on five multi-page document VQA benchmarks among open-weight models up to 10B and reduces sensitivity to page boundaries.
summary.zh: DocSEAM 在视觉编码器与语言模型间插入轻量模块，用局部三联页与中心锚定掩码注意力融合邻页信息，9B 模型在五个多页文档 VQA 基准上取得不超过 10B 参数开放权重模型中的 SOTA，并降低对分页边界的敏感度。

papers.title: Toward Agentic Robotics: A Large-Scale Study of Harness Design for Robot-Use Agents
papers.abstract: Recent vision-language models (VLMs) can act as robot-use agents that understand diverse scenes and control robots through policy code and tools. However, they predict 3D gripper poses poorly even with extended reasoning, struggling with precise manipulation. Vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action (WAM) models are the opposite: they execute fast, smooth control on trained tasks, yet fail under domain shifts or when tasks require long-horizon memory and reasoning. Agentic robots therefore combine VLM reasoning and perception with precise VLA/WAM control through a policy harness. Yet harness design spans thousands of configurations, shifting success by tens of points with the same models. Moreover, testing even one design takes thousands of rollouts at high API and GPU cost, so prior works often commit to a single design chosen from few alternatives. To guide harness design, we evaluate over 470,000 rollouts across eight simulation benchmarks, six VLMs, and 15 VLA/WAM checkpoints. Seven controlled studies show effective harnesses must adapt to both VLM and VLA/WAM capabilities. Our findings specify what structure the VLM's policy code needs, where VLA manipulation needs help from tools and policy code, and when to involve the VLM at test time. The reference recipe X-Harness shows that these findings compose without weight updates, lifting base policies up to $+42.8$ points across memory, reasoning, and domain shifts.

summary.en: X-Harness pairs VLM reasoning with VLA/WAM control via a policy harness; 470K+ rollouts across 8 benchmarks reveal harness design rules, lifting base policies up to +42.8 points on memory, reasoning, and domain shifts without weight updates.
summary.zh: X-Harness 通过策略框架把 VLM 推理与 VLA/WAM 精确控制结合，基于 47 万余次 rollout、8 个仿真基准、6 个 VLM 和 15 个 VLA/WAM 检查点的七项受控实验，揭示框架需适配双方能力，在记忆、推理与域偏移任务上无需权重更新即提升基线最高 42.8 个点。

papers.title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
papers.abstract: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet visual corruption can disrupt the resulting policies. We introduce HOG-WAM, which adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as structural supervision derived directly from demonstration images. An auxiliary HOG diffusion transformer (DiT) module reads RGB features through asymmetric attention, allowing its objective to shape the visual representation used for control. The module is used only during training and removed at inference, preserving FastWAM's RGB-to-action architecture. We evaluate four controlled observation corruptions through a visual-corruption extension of RoboTwin, termed RoboTwin-Plus; HOG-WAM achieves the highest success among the compared policies under all four. Mixed-noise success increases from 78.86% to 82.86% relative to FastWAM, with comparable performance on clean scenes. On LIBERO Plus, overall success increases from 74.49% to 75.26%, with the largest gain under sensor noise, from 74.14% to 78.89%. Across four Franka tasks, average success increases from 40% to 59% under clean observations and from 17% to 24% under noisy observations. A representation ablation favors combining RGB observations with auxiliary HOG prediction over replacing RGB with HOG. These findings support future-gradient prediction as complementary supervision for visually robust control, with larger absolute gains on physical tasks than in simulation. Code is available at https://github.com/iPPLab/HOG-WAM.

summary.en: HOG-WAM adds future HOG structural supervision to FastWAM via a training-only HOG DiT with asymmetric attention; mixed-noise success rises from 78.86% to 82.86% on RoboTwin-Plus and sensor-noise success from 74.14% to 78.89% on LIBERO Plus.
summary.zh: HOG-WAM 在 FastWAM 的 RGB-to-action 架构上加入未来 HOG 结构监督，训练时用 HOG DiT 通过非对称注意力读取 RGB 特征、推理时移除该模块；在 RoboTwin-Plus 混合噪声下成功率从 78.86% 提升到 82.86%，LIBERO Plus 传感器噪声下从 74.14% 提升到 78.89%，四个 Franka 任务的干净与含噪平均成功率分别从 40% 升到 59%、从 17% 升到 24%。

papers.title: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for image matting by transferring generative priors learned from large-scale pretraining. However, existing approaches largely rely on latent diffusion models, whose compressed representations and VAE-based reconstruction introduce a mismatch with the high-frequency precision required for matting. We present PixelMatte, a framework that adapts pretrained pixel-space diffusion transformers for high-fidelity image matting. We show that strong image-conditioned matting capabilities can be acquired even from a pure text-to-image model without paired image-to-image pretraining. Our approach reuses the backbone's native patch embedding to jointly process the input image, trimap, and noisy alpha matte as spatially aligned tokens, enabling direct pixel-space prediction without additional condition encoders or adapters. With pixel-accurate synthetic supervision and real-image fine-tuning, PixelMatte predicts alpha mattes in a single forward pass. Two lightweight calibration modules, LayerShift and High-Pass Refiner, further improve regional opacity accuracy and boundary fidelity. Experiments across four benchmarks and two distinct pixel diffusion backbones demonstrate substantial improvements over existing methods, reducing SAD and gradient errors by 24-44% relative to RenderMatte on P3M-500-NP and AM-2K, while achieving competitive performance on AIM-500 and RenderMatte-2K. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of pixel-space generative priors for precision-sensitive image matting. Project page: https://white-yc.github.io/pixelmatte/.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Project page: https://white-yc.github.io/pixelmatte/

summary.en: PixelMatte adapts pretrained pixel-space diffusion transformers to high-fidelity matting, jointly processing image, trimap, and noisy alpha via native patch embedding and predicting alpha in one pass; LayerShift and High-Pass Refiner further refine results, cutting SAD and gradient errors by 24-44% versus RenderMatte on P3M-500-NP and AM-2K.
summary.zh: PixelMatte 把预训练的像素空间扩散 Transformer 用于高保真抠图，复用原生 patch embedding 将图像、trimap 和噪声 alpha 作为空间对齐 token 联合处理，单次前向即可预测 alpha，并用 LayerShift 与 High-Pass Refiner 提升区域不透明度与边界精度；在 P3M-500-NP 与 AM-2K 上相比 RenderMatte 降低 SAD 与梯度误差 24-44%。

papers.title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
papers.abstract: Robots should adapt to unfamiliar environments and acquire new skills through interaction, then execute those skills efficiently with practice. Vision-language-action policies provide efficient control, but often need additional human demonstrations to handle unfamiliar settings; reasoning agents can discover solutions using broad prior knowledge and robot-control APIs, but repeated deliberation and repair are costly. Inspired by human learning through reasoning and practice, we propose RoboEvo$^2$, a framework for recursive harness-policy co-evolution. In Policy-to-Harness (P2H) evolution, policy failures guide a coding agent to search complementary Code, Code+ICL, and Code+Policy routes, consolidating verified solutions into reusable skills, routing strategies, and experience memory. In Harness-to-Policy (H2P) evolution, verified trajectories provide supervised training, while Counterfactual Preference Distillation (CPD) teaches the policy to favor successful corrections over failures from the same starting state. The improved policy provides stronger motor skills for subsequent search, while its remaining failures redirect harness evolution, closing the reciprocal loop. Through recursive co-evolution without additional human demonstrations, RoboEvo$^2$ improves standalone success from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5% on LIBERO-PRO, with similar gains and reduced agentic costs on RoboTwin C2R. Further experiments demonstrate autonomous task acquisition, cross-embodiment harness transfer, and 95.0% hybrid success on the Unitree G1-D. Our models and code will be publicly released.

summary.en: RoboEvo$^2$ recursively co-evolves a coding harness and VLA policy via policy-to-harness search and harness-to-policy distillation, raising LIBERO-PRO success from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5%.
summary.zh: RoboEvo$^2$ 通过由 policy 到 harness 的编码搜索与由 harness 到 policy 的监督训练及反事实偏好蒸馏实现递归协同进化，在 LIBERO-PRO 上将独立成功率从 11.0% 提至 84.1%，混合成功率从 30.4% 提至 90.5%，Unitree G1-D 上混合成功率达 95.0%。

orgs.name: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
papers.abstract: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at aim-uofa.github.io/WorldReforge/.

summary.en: WorldReforge builds the 62k-trajectory Reforge dataset by perturbing reference grasps and adds Interaction Alignment and Surface Correspondence training signals, cutting Cosmos3 Nano's object-trajectory error by 35.0% on unseen objects and action-divergence error by 43.3%.
summary.zh: WorldReforge 用扰动参考抓取得到的 62k 条模拟轨迹构建 Reforge 数据集，并引入 Interaction Alignment 与 Surface Correspondence 两种训练信号，使 Cosmos3 Nano 在未见物体上的物体轨迹误差降低 35.0%，两动作结果差异预测误差降低 43.3%。

papers.title: Playfulness as Feedback for Agentic Game Development
papers.abstract: Coding agents can generate runnable games from natural-language descriptions. However, a runnable game does not guarantee an excellent gameplay experience for players. In our view, a playful game should provide 1) reliable core functionality, 2) appealing visual design and assets, and 3) rich gameplay that supports exploration and progression. How agents can improve these aspects of playfulness remains underexplored. In our work, we propose Play2Evolve, a recursive game development framework with three stages: Initialization, Refinement, and Evolution. Using playfulness as feedback, agents playtest the game and diagnose issues in its functionality, visual presentation, and gameplay. Their feedback guides bug fixes and asset improvements. It also helps agents propose new gameplay and aesthetic goals for continued game evolution. To enrich game materials, we combine a video generation model with code to create appealing static and dynamic assets and integrate them into interactive gameplay. Finally, Play2Evolve achieves state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods, scoring 60.05 on GameCraft-Bench compared with 50.81 after Game Initialization and 52.46 for Play2Code. Human overall-quality ratings reach 3.67, compared with 2.38 and 2.43, respectively. Our code will be released at https://github.com/showlab/Play2Evolve.

summary.en: Play2Evolve uses playfulness as feedback in a recursive initialize-refine-evolve framework where agents playtest games, diagnose functionality, visuals and gameplay, and pair video generation with code; it scores 60.05 on GameCraft-Bench versus 50.81 and 52.46, with human ratings of 3.67.
summary.zh: Play2Evolve 以可玩性为反馈，用三段式递归框架（初始化、精炼、进化）让智能体试玩诊断功能、视觉与玩法问题，并结合视频生成模型产出素材，在 GameCraft-Bench 上得 60.05，高于 Game Initialization 的 50.81 和 Play2Code 的 52.46，人工整体质量评分 3.67。

orgs.name: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
papers.abstract: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs from video recordings, and several benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate them. However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to $N \times M$ integrations when evaluating $N$ methods on $M$ benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark. Moreover, Real2SimLab provides a pipeline to create training data and reward annotations for real-to-simulation methods. Our pipeline carefully avoids data contamination by filtering out the video recordings that exist in benchmarks. For each video recording, a program is first produced, and then our pipeline computes its reward with the same code that Real2SimLab uses for evaluation. So far, it supports 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods on 6 benchmarks. Both the platform and Awesome-Real2Sim, our research map of nearly 300 real-to-simulation papers, are open source, and we invite the Real2SimHub community to build them together.

summary.en: Real2SimLab is a unified platform that evaluates real-to-simulation methods by running their generated programs and scoring outputs with each benchmark's own scorer, covering 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods on 6 benchmarks, plus a contamination-filtered data and reward pipeline.
summary.zh: Real2SimLab 统一评测平台通过运行各方法生成的仿真程序，并调用各基准自带的评分器打分，避免了 N 种方法在 M 个基准上的 N×M 次集成；它支持 6 个基准上 47 个编程 agent 和 5 种非 agent 方法，还提供训练数据与奖励标注流水线，并通过过滤基准已有视频避免数据污染。

papers.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
papers.abstract: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into 65,000 trajectories (116 h) and 325,000 episodes (578 h) in total. Even with arms attached, DexEngine tracks objects more accurately than prior floating-hand methods and runs over 10x faster than RL-based ones. Policies trained on our data far outperform those trained on the same clips without physics correction or with the arms attached after a floating-hand correction, showing that fine-tuning data need physics correction. Mid-training on our data further improves them at equal fine-tuning budget, in simulation and on a real robot.
papers.comment: Project page: https://wongyun-yu.github.io/dexengine/ Code: https://github.com/wongyun-yu/DexEngine Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Wongyun/DexEngine

summary.en: DexEngine is a simulation pipeline that retargets human hand-object demonstrations into physically executable arm-hand trajectories via reachability placement, arm fitting, and residual RL correction, producing 65,000 trajectories (116 h) across four dexterous hands and yielding policies that outperform uncorrected data baselines in simulation and on a real robot.
summary.zh: DexEngine 用仿真流水线把人类手物操作数据转成整臂-手可执行轨迹：先定位到可达位置、拟合手臂运动，再用残差强化学习在物理仿真中校正。从九个数据集为四种灵巧手各生成约 5,200 条片段，扩充为 65,000 条轨迹（116 小时）和 325,000 个 episode（578 小时），物体跟踪精度优于浮动手方法且比 RL 方法快 10 倍以上，训练的策略在仿真与真机上均优于未做物理校正的数据。

papers.title: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
papers.abstract: Accurate 3D surface reconstruction from unposed images remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision. Recent feed-forward pointmap methods eliminate the need for camera poses but inherently produce discrete, sparse representations. In this paper, we present a generalizable pipeline that directly recovers continuous, high-fidelity 3D surfaces from unposed images by seamlessly integrating pointmap- and ray-based representations. Our approach first extracts explicit geometric priors using a pre-trained pointmap model. A query-view-centric selection module then identifies geometrically relevant reference views via a robust surfel voting mechanism. Next, a cross-attention regressor bridges target query rays with reference features to estimate a continuous coarse surface. Lastly, a raylet-based module aggregates local 3D features to carve out high-frequency details and analytical normals. Trained as a single foundation model on 9 diverse datasets, our method demonstrates exceptional zero-shot generalization on 6 unseen datasets, clearly surpassing state-of-the-art baselines in geometric accuracy and detail preservation.

summary.en: FoundSurface combines pointmap and ray representations to reconstruct continuous, high-fidelity 3D surfaces from unposed images, using a pointmap prior, cross-attention coarse regression, and raylet refinement, outperforming baselines in zero-shot generalization on 6 unseen datasets.
summary.zh: FoundSurface 将 pointmap 与 ray 表示结合，从无位姿图像直接重建连续高保真三维表面：先用 pointmap 模型提取几何先验，再经查询视角选择与 cross-attention 回归粗表面，最后用 raylet 模块恢复高频细节与解析法线，在 6 个未见数据集上零样本泛化优于现有方法。

papers.title: Looped Models are Fast Multi-Token Predictors
papers.abstract: Looped language models can adapt computation for predicting a token without a proportional rescaling in unique model parameters by adjusting the number of loops. This property has been used for self-speculative decoding, taking shallow loops as fast drafters and deep loops as verifiers, which is effective since drafting still uses full parameters. In this paper, we show that shallow loops can be also predictive of several future tokens and leverage this to drastically accelerate the inference of looped language models. To that end, we present Floodgates, a simple self-speculative decoding method that appends a block of mask tokens as a suffix and learns via low-rank adaptation to draft these tokens in parallel. Across seven models, five benchmarks, a range of batch sizes, and both greedy and sampled decoding, Floodgates is the fastest lossless decoding method in most cases, attaining up to 7.5x acceleration. Through analysis, we show that this speedup is enabled by all-depth training of looped models, with the shallow drafter's ability to leverage full-depth computation by conditioning on deep prefix cache evaluated during verification.

summary.zh: Floodgates 是面向循环语言模型的自投机解码方法：在序列尾部附加掩码 token 块，用低秩适配让浅层循环并行草拟多个未来 token、深层循环验证，在七个模型、五个基准上多数情况取得无损解码最快速度，最高加速 7.5 倍。
summary.en: Floodgates is a self-speculative decoding method for looped language models that appends a mask-token block and uses low-rank adaptation to draft multiple future tokens in parallel with shallow loops, reaching up to 7.5x lossless speedup.

papers.title: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation
papers.abstract: Camera-controlled video generation re-renders a video along a target camera trajectory, yet moving the camera around an object, the most natural way to change the viewpoint of an object-centric scene, remains difficult. Existing methods condition either on camera parameters, which are scale-ambiguous in monocular video, or on explicit geometry such as warped point clouds or depth, which breaks down under large viewpoint changes. We present AnyCam, a method that represents the camera with an anchor object in the scene: we reconstruct it in 3D and render it along the target trajectory, a camera signal that is scale-aware, view-complete and easy to specify relative to the object. A video diffusion model transfers the content and dynamics of the source video to the new viewpoint. Its H-Concat layout aligns source and target frames in time, so the model can be distilled into AnyCam-AR, a streaming few-step generator for on-the-fly camera control. Both models are trained on paired videos with pixel-aligned anchor renderings from multi-camera videos and static-scene captures. Experiments on diverse datasets and trajectories show that AnyCam performs favorably against camera-controlled video generation and 3D reconstruction methods in camera control and visual quality.

summary.en: AnyCam represents the camera via a reconstructed anchor object rendered along the target trajectory, then transfers source video content and dynamics with a video diffusion model; its H-Concat layout enables a streaming few-step generator and outperforms camera-controlled video generation and 3D reconstruction baselines.
summary.zh: AnyCam 以场景中的锚定物体来表示相机：先重建该物体的 3D 模型并沿目标轨迹渲染，得到尺度明确、视角完整且易于指定的相机信号，再用视频扩散模型将源视频的内容与动态迁移到新视角；H-Concat 布局对齐源帧与目标帧的时间，模型可蒸馏为流式少步生成器 AnyCam-AR。在多数据集与轨迹上，相机控制与视觉质量优于相机控制视频生成和 3D 重建方法。

papers.title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene address this, but when they meet conditions that earlier attempts did not cover, revising them requires the measured effects of earlier actions. We therefore propose SEEK, an agentic framework that retains both, enabling robots to improve across attempts while keeping the underlying model fixed. To adapt retained knowledge to the current scene, SEEK adopts a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) that encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current observations. As the robot executes these procedures, SEEK records the measured effects of its actions, including those from failed attempts, in a Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB). Where a retained procedure applies, it acts without a model request; where it meets a condition it does not cover, this evidence guides its revision. On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks. On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests. https://zeyangguan.github.io/SEEK-Agentic-Robot-Manipulation/

summary.en: SEEK retains execution knowledge across attempts via a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy and a Persistent Action-Effect Bank; on RoboDojo's 42 tasks ten attempts raise score from 27.0 to 54.4 and success from 19.7% to 48.0%, with 77.6% fewer GPT-6.2 Astra requests.
summary.zh: SEEK 是可跨尝试保留执行知识的机器人操作框架：Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) 将操作编码为可执行程序，并依据当前观测决定动作；Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB) 记录动作实测效果，用于修订程序；在 RoboDojo 全部 42 项任务上，十次尝试将平均任务分从 27.0 提升至 54.4、成功率从 19.7% 提升至 48.0%，在 34 项任务上使用 GPT-6.2 Astra 五次尝试达到 80.1，而直接调用同一模型为 49.6，模型请求减少 77.6%。

papers.title: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos
papers.abstract: Embodied agents operating around people must not only recognize social cues, but also decide when the available evidence is sufficient, whether to intervene, and how to respond without violating social norms. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate these abilities in isolation or with access to completed videos, obscuring where an online social decision fails. We introduce AIRIS, a causal streaming benchmark that formulates social embodied intelligence as a time-anchored chain of Attention, Intention, Reaction, and Interaction (A-I-R-I). AIRIS contains 8,000 expert-curated questions grounded in 357 egocentric clips across 11 context categories and 36 capability dimensions. At each query, models receive only the observation prefix available at that time; decision-aware metrics reward calibrated waiting and complete reactions while penalizing premature commitment. Evaluating 45 proprietary and open-source general-purpose, embodied, streaming-video, and omni-modal models reveals fragmented and temporally miscalibrated competence. General-purpose VLMs excel at passive cue grounding and intent recognition, whereas embodied specialists lead on isolated reaction sub-decisions; yet across all families, models frequently guess intents before sufficient evidence emerges and fail to jointly align intervention timing, action domain, and concrete execution within the same episode. AIRIS thus provides a diagnostic foundation for bridging the gap between passive social perception and reliable embodied interaction.

summary.en: AIRIS is a causal streaming benchmark that decomposes social embodied intelligence into a time-anchored Attention-Intention-Reaction-Interaction chain, with 8,000 questions over 357 egocentric clips where models see only the observation prefix; evaluating 45 models reveals fragmented, temporally miscalibrated competence.
summary.zh: AIRIS 是一个因果流式基准，将社交具身智能拆解为 Attention、Intention、Reaction、Interaction 的时间锚定链条，基于 357 段第一视角视频构建 8,000 道题，模型只能看到查询时刻之前的观察前缀；评测 45 个专有与开源模型后发现能力碎片化且时间校准失准。

papers.title: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
papers.abstract: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures revisit layer parameters across depths. This design increases effective depth without adding parameters. Recent looped MoE studies report substantial gains over the standard MoE at matched budgets (parameters, FLOPs and KV cache). However, the reported gains still confound parameter revisit with other design choices, e.g., network shape and residual scale. We ask, what does parameter revisit itself buy? Using matched non-revisit controls, we find that parameter revisit itself buys almost nothing. We argue that revisit only offers a freedom an MoE already has, i.e., trading experts for depth (more layers, fewer experts each) at fixed parameters. First, at matched budgets, we decompose the state-of-the-art looped recipe, with revisit last. A non-revisit control retains all the gain. Most comes from network shape, and the rest from residual scale. We prove this scale acts as a lower learning rate on revisited layers. This helps under AdamW's uneven layer step sizes, but disappears under Muon, which keeps them nearly equal. Second, beyond matched budgets, we evaluate revisit by adding compute at fixed parameters. One extra visit gains more than doubling the experts. Yet without revisit, a deeper standard MoE at equal parameters and compute obtains 90.2% of that gain under Muon. Overall, gains come from network shape, the optimizer and added compute, which a standard MoE can adopt. Accordingly, we propose LoopTitan-Base as a stronger MoE baseline. Under Muon, it matches the strongest looped recipe without revisit or residual scale. We open-source LoopTitan and release 17 pretrained models (including LoopTitan-Base and the control). Our experiment record is public as GitHub issues, with predictions pre-registered and the full exploration history kept. This is our Phase 1 technical report, laying the foundation for follow-up studies.
papers.comment: 45 pages. Phase 1 technical report. Project page: https://datamllab.github.io/LoopTitan/ ; code: https://github.com/datamllab/LoopTitan ; models: https://huggingface.co/NaturalScale

summary.en: Matched non-revisit controls show parameter revisit in looped MoE buys almost nothing; gains come from network shape and residual scale (a lower learning rate on revisited layers under AdamW). LoopTitan-Base, a non-revisit baseline under Muon, matches the strongest looped recipe, with 17 pretrained models released.
summary.zh: 用匹配预算的非重访对照组拆解 looped MoE，发现参数重访本身几乎没有收益，增益主要来自网络形状与残差缩放（相当于对重访层降低学习率），在 Muon 下残差缩放收益消失；据此提出无重访的 LoopTitan-Base，在 Muon 下匹配最强循环方案，并开源 17 个预训练模型。

papers.title: Target-Part Preference Optimization for Part-Aware 3D Generation
papers.abstract: Part-aware 3D generation requires not only globally plausible objects but also complete, well-separated semantic parts, yet high-quality part decompositions remain too scarce to support large-scale supervised fine-tuning. We study whether preference fine-tuning based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) can adapt a pretrained part-aware generator from limited part-annotated data without architectural changes. We rank candidates generated with different random seeds against ground-truth (GT) geometric metrics, and select the (object, target-part) examples with the largest across-seed quality gap. Each selected example stores a seed pair whose two flow trajectories share one clean GT compositional latent and differ only in Gaussian noise. We derive a reference-relative target-block preference loss from FlowDPO that compares the two trajectories against a frozen reference model. GT flow-matching losses on the target block and complete part set provide absolute supervision, while only the diffusion transformer (DiT) is updated. Human-ranked controls test an alternative ordering source, and synthetic cropping provides controlled loser targets that are incomplete by construction. Among the three training-set scales, the medium-scale setting gives the strongest result on held-out Objaverse and outperforms both the pretrained generator and the reported direct supervised fine-tuning baseline on the multi-part aggregate. Further analysis shows sensitivity to pair ordering, target-part coverage, and the balance between pairwise and GT supervision. Cross-dataset experiments show less consistent gains under distribution shift.

summary.zh: Target-Part Preference Optimization 用 FlowDPO 式偏好微调改造预训练的部件感知 3D 生成器，按随机种子与 GT 几何指标筛选部件质量差距最大的样本对，仅更新 DiT；在 Objaverse 上多部件聚合指标整体超过预训练模型与监督微调基线，跨数据集收益不稳定。
summary.en: Target-Part Preference Optimization fine-tunes a pretrained part-aware 3D generator with a FlowDPO-style target-block preference loss, selecting seed pairs by GT geometric metric gaps and updating only the DiT; it beats the pretrained generator and supervised fine-tuning baselines on Objaverse multi-part aggregates, with weaker gains under distribution shift.

papers.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
papers.abstract: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts. Across MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol, we isolate the effects of individual harness design choices by evaluating each against a recency-truncation baseline within a shared agent framework. For context management, we find that preserving individually accessible records of past attempts is more effective than maintaining a rolling summary, with context folding performing best across all six settings and improving upon the baseline by up to 19.2%. For skill management, selectively discarding persistently unused lessons is more effective on average than consolidating them or promoting them to standing rules. Building on these findings, we combine context folding and skill deletion in MLEvolver, which achieves a 72.7% medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite and a 94% $\mathrm{fast}_1$ score on KernelBench Level 3, substantially outperforming AIDE and OpenEvolve under the same inference budget. Overall, our study distills design principles for preserving experimental history and curating reusable lessons in autoresearch harnesses, paving the way for agents that turn accumulated experience into sustained progress.

summary.en: A systematic study of autoresearch harness design shows context folding beats recency truncation by up to 19.2%, and MLEvolver, combining context folding with skill deletion, reaches 72.7% medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite and 94% fast1 on KernelBench Level 3.
summary.zh: 系统研究 autoresearch agent 的 harness 设计：对比上下文管理与技能管理策略，在 MLE-Bench 和 KernelBench 上发现 context folding 比近期截断基线最高提升 19.2%，结合技能删除的 MLEvolver 在 MLE-Bench Lite 达 72.7% 奖牌率、KernelBench Level 3 达 94% fast1。

papers.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
papers.abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints. Independent checks use simulation state and episode records to assess outcomes and task requirements, with stronger checks of geometry, coverage, or placement. It comprises 250 manually validated tasks across 11 types in five groups and 27 indoor environments, covering object and room search, counting, geometric judgments, direction reasoning, and relocation. Human evaluators achieve 84% strict task success on 100 sampled tasks, with every correct outcome satisfying the required checks. Across seven frontier vision-language models, we identify two complementary failure modes: correct outcomes with unmet task requirements, and incorrect outcomes despite passing stronger checks. Oracle-input diagnostics show that more complete target observations and calibrated feedback improve final spatial judgments.

summary.en: ROAM-Bench evaluates embodied active spatial intelligence under robot motion and collision constraints with 250 tasks across 27 indoor environments, using simulation states and episode records to independently verify outcomes and task requirements; humans reach 84% strict success while seven frontier VLMs show two complementary failure modes.
summary.zh: ROAM-Bench 在机器人运动与碰撞约束下评测具身主动空间智能，含 5 组 11 类共 250 个任务、27 个室内环境，用仿真状态和 episode 记录独立核验结果与任务要求；人类严格成功率达 84%，七个前沿 VLM 暴露出两类互补失败模式。

papers.title: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Multi-scale architectures are widely adopted in all-in-one image restoration (AIO-IR) to capture larger-scale context at low-resolution stages and refine details at high-resolution (HR) stages. However, processing spatially large feature maps at HR stages incurs substantial computational costs and memory traffic, making efficient HR processing challenging. To address this challenge, we propose High-resolution Global-Local Restoration (HiGLR), an efficient multi-scale AIO-IR network grounded in an analysis of spatial redundancy in self-attention and convolutional feed-forward networks (ConvFFNs). Specifically, this analysis identifies three key redundancies: per-query readout at the finest-scale stage, key routing across neighboring queries at intermediate stages, and spatial mixing in the expanded feature spaces of ConvFFNs. Accordingly, HiGLR replaces costly self-attention at the finest-scale stage with a learned input-independent kernel. At intermediate stages, we propose a Block-Routed Hybrid Attention, which combines coarse-scale dense attention with fine-scale block-sparse attention over value residuals relative to coarse summaries, and shares routing indices across neighboring queries. We further introduce a Dual-Space FFN that performs spatial mixing in a compact space and pointwise nonlinear transformation in an expanded space, enabling efficient kernel fusion. Combining these designs, HiGLR achieves state-of-the-art performance while delivering up to a $4.24\times$ inference speedup over existing methods.

summary.en: HiGLR analyzes spatial redundancy in self-attention and ConvFFNs, replacing finest-scale attention with a learned input-independent kernel and adding Block-Routed Hybrid Attention and a Dual-Space FFN, reaching state-of-the-art all-in-one image restoration with up to 4.24x inference speedup.
summary.zh: HiGLR 通过分析自注意力与 ConvFFN 的空间冗余，用输入无关核替换最细尺度注意力、提出 Block-Routed Hybrid Attention 与 Dual-Space FFN，在 all-in-one 图像复原上取得 SOTA，推理速度最高提升 4.24 倍。

papers.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Scattered Views for Coherent 3D World Generation
papers.abstract: Generating coherent and explorable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap is a fundamental and long-standing challenge in computer vision, which existing geometry-aware methods fail to address. Meanwhile, existing image- and video-based methods may generate unseen regions but produce inconsistent geometry across views. To bridge this gap, we present WorldBridge, a framework for coherent and controllable 3D world generation under scattered images with little or no visual overlap. WorldBridge encodes scattered references into a global scene context to guide geometry and appearance generation across views. Our temporal and spatial reference attention mechanism further enhances the fidelity of temporal references along the target trajectory and supports flexible spatial references outside it. A plug-and-play latent-reference consistency strategy improves reference fidelity through reprojection-guided test-time optimization. We also introduce the WorldBridge benchmark suite to evaluate 3D world generation from scattered, low-overlap references, which is rarely explored by current benchmarks. Both qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate that our method enables controllable and coherent 3D world generation, surpassing the existing state-of-the-art solutions. Our project page is available at https://davidyan2001.github.io/WorldBridge/.

summary.en: WorldBridge encodes scattered, low-overlap references into a global scene context with spatio-temporal reference attention and reprojection-guided latent consistency, enabling coherent controllable 3D world generation and outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
summary.zh: WorldBridge 将稀疏且几乎无重叠的参考图像编码为全局场景上下文，结合时空参考注意力与重投影引导的潜参考一致性优化，实现连贯可控的 3D 世界生成，并推出低重叠参考的基准套件，性能超越现有 SOTA。

papers.title: Skeptic: Grounding Failure Diagnosis for Robot Skill Discovery
papers.abstract: Robot agents discover reusable skills by revising programs from execution feedback and retaining experience for later tasks. This process can fail when an agent treats an unsuccessful program as evidence that the task is physically impossible, ending exploration with revision budget remaining. We study this failure in Qwen3.8-27B and examine two decisions that shape skill discovery: I) how execution failures are diagnosed, and II) which lessons enter the shared skill library. Failure diagnosis requires the agent to reconstruct physical action effects from multimodal traces, while independent reproduction of a proposed repair does not require adequate task performance from its source program. We introduce Skeptic, a training-free protocol that uses measured action outcomes to guide repair and measured task success to govern skill admission. A grounded event log reports action effects and object end states from depth images and proprioception, separating sensor observations from inferred diagnoses. Verified promotion adds a development-success requirement on the source program to the existing independent reproduction check. Across 60 audited tasks, the mean number of tasks with false impossibility judgments decreases from 19.5 to 8.5 per campaign. On 80 LIBERO-Pro tasks and seven Robosuite tasks, Skeptic improves held-out success by 14.9 and 11.7 percentage points, with frozen model weights and the same program-revision budget.

summary.en: Skeptic grounds repair in measured action outcomes and admits skills by measured task success via a depth-and-proprioception event log; false-impossibility tasks drop from 19.5 to 8.5, and held-out success rises 14.9 and 11.7 points on LIBERO-Pro and Robosuite.
summary.zh: Skeptic 用实测动作效果引导修复、以实测任务成功准入技能，并用带深度与本体感知的事件日志区分观测与诊断；在 60 个审计任务上，误判物理不可行的任务数从 19.5 降至 8.5，LIBERO-Pro 与 Robosuite 留出成功率分别提升 14.9 和 11.7 个百分点。

papers.title: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity
papers.abstract: To avoid the quadratic cost of dense attention over long contexts, models such as DeepSeek-V4 and Hy4 have turned natively sparse, and speculative decoding, which matters most where decoding is slowest, increasingly runs on them. Their drafters, however, still keep a context cache of their own, over the whole prompt or a sliding window. Beyond memory, such a cache costs prefill time, prefix-cache hits and decode concurrency. Drafters that read the target's cache avoid one of their own, but settle only which cache, not which positions, and still read everything or a recent window. Neither rule is made for the query at hand, and computing a selection per query in the drafter would cost more as the context grows. Yet a natively sparse target already picks positions for each query, over a cache it keeps anyway. Both of the drafter's choices are therefore already made, and paid for, by the target: its cache and its selection. We measure how far one selection carries: made a step early, it still covers close to nine tenths of what each later token selects on DS-V4.1-Flash. We present DFly2, a block-parallel drafter that shares the target's sparsity. Each draft layer reads the KV its paired target layer cached (KV sharing), at the positions that layer's indexer selected, a fixed number anywhere in the context (Index sharing). DFly2 thus runs no scoring pass and keeps no cache of its own. On DS-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash and Hy4~flash, whose sparse attention and architecture differ, it accepts more tokens per step than DFlash and DSpark trained on the same recipe, over general, long-context and agentic benchmarks. Its margin over the stronger baseline widens from 3.9%-10.5% on general workloads to 10.0%-31.5% on long-context and agentic ones. At high concurrency on DS-V4.1-Flash, at matched per-user decode speed, its throughput is 62% and 81% higher on two 64K sets.

papers.title: Look Back: Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual World Models
papers.abstract: Agents in complex, stochastic environments must contend with dynamics that can exceed their world models' predictive capacity and randomness that obscure the consequences of their actions. We hypothesize that, compared to imagining entirely new trajectories in such complex environments, it can be easier to transform observed trajectories with alternative actions. Counterfactual world models condition on observations to predict alternative outcomes under the same underlying environmental randomness, using experience as a reference for predicting action-dependent changes. We present a policy gradient estimator, REINFORCE Look Back (RLB), that uses counterfactual returns as baselines to distinguish action effects from environmental luck, and prove conditions for unbiasedness and variance reduction. In settings where environmental evolution is harder to predict than action-induced changes, we show that counterfactual world models are easier to learn and support better policy learning than ordinary world models. Our findings suggest that counterfactual thinking can help agents learn effective behavior without independently reproducing the full complexity of their worlds.

summary.en: REINFORCE Look Back (RLB) uses counterfactual world models to predict outcomes under alternative actions and counterfactual returns as baselines, provably reducing variance and separating action effects from environmental luck.
summary.zh: REINFORCE Look Back (RLB) 策略梯度估计器，用反事实世界模型预测同一环境随机性下替换动作后的结果，并以反事实回报作为基线分离动作效应与环境运气，证明其无偏性与方差缩减条件。在环境演化比动作影响更难预测时，反事实世界模型比普通世界模型更易学习并带来更好的策略学习。

papers.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
papers.abstract: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision. Simulation-based synthesis faces a substantial visual gap relative to real environments, while video-only generation struggles to maintain physically consistent interactions and provide aligned action labels. We present DemoFoundry, an automated framework that couples coding agents with generative rendering to synthesize photorealistic and physically grounded robot demonstrations. Coding agents both construct aligned real--proxy video pairs from existing robot episodes to train a video renderer and write executable interaction programs to generate new demonstrations. Given a scene reference and task instruction, an agent reconstructs task-relevant geometry and writes a control program without requiring target-task human demonstrations. Program execution in a physics simulator produces proxy videos with aligned robot states and actions. The video renderer translates these proxy videos into scene-consistent, photorealistic observations, reducing the need for detailed appearance modeling in each scene. Automated task-execution checks select successful trajectories for rendering and policy learning. Experiments show improved visual quality and action--video consistency. Policies trained on the generated demonstrations outperform raw-simulation training and approach the performance of training on an equal number of real demonstrations.

summary.en: DemoFoundry uses coding agents and generative rendering to synthesize photorealistic and physically grounded robot demonstrations, achieving policy performance close to training on real data.
summary.zh: DemoFoundry利用编程智能体与生成式渲染技术合成了具备真实视觉与物理基础的机器人示范数据，通过构建对齐的真实-代理视频对并结合物理仿真执行程序生成数据，在策略训练中接近了等量真实示范的性能。

papers.title: You Only Look Multiple Times: YoloMT, a Real-Time Streaming Model on a T4
papers.abstract: We introduce a new model for real-time streaming captioning on a single GPU. YoloMT is a 449.8M-parameter streaming captioner that provides Pareto-frontier performance among generative vision models in its class. Distilled from a 27B teacher by SFT and GRPO, it leads every model under 1B parameters on OVO-Bench, MVBench, StreamingBench and Video-MME, answered from its captions, and beats LFM2.5-VL-1.6B and SmolVLM2-2.2B. YoloMT is designed to read more frames cheaply and make them informative, encoding each frame once and caching it as 16 tokens. This allows the model to incorporate and infer from past frames without additional vision passes, making it efficient and effective. We also provide a detailed recipe for training YoloMT, with its stages and data, as well as ablations that demonstrate the contribution of each component.

papers.title: iMFPO: Improving Mean Flow Policy Optimization with Drift-Aware Velocity Alignment for Embodied Control
papers.abstract: Flow-based generative policies offer expressive action modeling for embodied control, yet achieving efficient one-step generation under reward-driven policy optimization remains challenging. In particular, evolving action distributions during online reinforcement learning may introduce inconsistencies between instantaneous-velocity learning and interval-averaged action generation. To address this challenge, we propose iMFPO, a one-step generative policy optimization framework with decoupled velocity learning and drift-aware velocity alignment. A shared interval-conditioned actor supports instantaneous-velocity supervision and interval-averaged action generation. JVP-corrected velocity regression is jointly optimized with reward-driven policy objectives, with action-level guidance from a frozen PPO teacher during training. At inference, iMFPO directly generates actions through interval-averaged velocity prediction, achieving one-step control without iterative flow integration. Across Go2, G1, H1, and Spot, zero-latent evaluation yields mean returns of 35.69, 34.44, 416.23, and 29.86. On Go2, action-generation latency drops from 15.57 ms to 0.41 ms relative to 64-step RFPO. Code: https://github.com/AIGeeksGroup/iMFPO. Website: https://aigeeksgroup.github.io/iMFPO.

summary.en: IMFPO achieves efficient one-step generative policy optimization for embodied control via decoupled velocity learning and drift-aware velocity alignment, reducing action-generation latency on Go2 from 15.57 ms to 0.41 ms compared to 64-step RFPO.
summary.zh: iMFPO通过解耦速度学习和漂移感知速度对齐，实现了具身控制的高效一步生成策略优化。在Go2、G1、H1和Spot上评估取得了显著回报，在Go2上动作生成延迟相比64步RFPO从15.57毫秒降至0.41毫秒。

papers.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
papers.abstract: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks. Two unified models, BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B, each lose accuracy on eight tasks. On VSTAR, adding a generated image to the same planning hint lowers accuracy by 10.47 points. Repeated image edits yield different outcomes across tasks. ChartQAPro and MathVista stay below their no-generation baselines, while ERQA gains three points after ten edits.

papers.title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
papers.abstract: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide visual richness but flatten content into difficult-to-edit pixels. A hybrid system can combine these strengths, but must coordinate interdependent decisions across content, layout, and appearance.
